bookInfo.author: Xue Juzheng et al.

title.zh: 卷一百〇五 漢書7: 宗室列傳二
title.en: Volume 105 Book of Later Jin 7: Biographies 2 - Imperial Family
title.raw: 卷一百〇五 漢書7: 宗室列傳二 Volume 105 Book of Later Jin 7: Biographies 2 - Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 蔡王信，高祖之從弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Cai Xin was a collateral younger male relative of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cai Xin was a cousin of Later Han Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 少從軍，漸至龍武小校。

translations.literal: In youth he followed the army and gradually rose to junior officer of the Dragon Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the army young and slowly worked his way up to a junior post in the Dragon Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 漢祖鎮并州，為興捷軍都將，領龔州刺史、檢校太保。

translations.literal: When the Han founder held Bingzhou, he served as commander-in-chief of the Xingjie Army, and concurrently held the posts of prefect of Gongzhou and honorary Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Zhiyuan governed Bingzhou, Xin became commander of the Xingjie Army and also served as prefect of Gong and honorary Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 國初，為侍衛馬軍都指揮使、檢校太傅兼義成軍節度使，尋移鎮許州，加太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was made commander of the palace horse guard, honorary Grand Mentor and concurrently military governor of the Yicheng circuit; soon he was transferred to hold Xuzhou, and was further given Grand Marshal and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he commanded the palace horse guard, served as honorary Grand Mentor and military governor of Yicheng, then was shifted to Xuzhou with the added titles of Grand Marshal and vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 高祖寢疾大漸，楊邠受密旨遣信赴鎮，信即時戒路，不得奉辭，雨泣而去。

translations.literal: When Gaozu's illness grew grave, Yang Bin received a secret order to send Xin back to his command; Xin at once made ready to depart, could not take formal leave, and went away weeping in the rain.
translations.idiomatic: As Gaozu lay dying, Yang Bin carried a secret order to send Xin back to his post; Xin set out at once without a farewell audience and left in tears through the rain.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor took the throne, Xin was given the additional title of honorary Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yin succeeded, Xin was made honorary Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 關輔賊平，就加侍中。

translations.literal: When the rebels in the Guanzhong region were pacified, he was thereupon made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Guanzhong rebels were crushed, he received the post of Palace Attendant on the spot.

sentences.zh: 信性昏懦，黷貨無厭，喜行酷法。

translations.literal: Xin's nature was dull and timid; he was insatiable in corrupt gain and delighted in harsh punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was stupid and spineless, greedy beyond satiety, and fond of cruel law.

sentences.zh: 掌禁軍時，左右有犯罪者，召其妻子，對之臠割，令自食其肉，或從足支解至首，血流盈前，而命樂對酒，無仁湣之色。

translations.literal: While he commanded the forbidden troops, when attendants committed offenses he would summon their wives and children, cut them to pieces before their eyes, and make them eat their own flesh; or he would dismember them from the feet up to the head, blood filling the ground before him, yet he would order music and drink wine opposite them, with no look of pity or compassion.
translations.idiomatic: While commanding the imperial guard, if a subordinate broke the law he would call in the man's wife and children, hack them apart before his eyes, and force him to eat their flesh—or slice him from foot to head until blood pooled at his feet—then order music and drink across the carnage without a trace of mercy.

sentences.zh: 未嘗接延賓客。

translations.literal: He never once received or entertained guests.
translations.idiomatic: He never entertained guests.

sentences.zh: 在鎮日，聚斂無度，會高祖山陵梓宮經由境上，信率掠吏民，以備迎奉，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: During his days in command he extorted without limit; it happened that Gaozu's mountain tomb and the imperial coffin passed through his territory, and Xin led the plunder of officials and commoners to prepare for the welcoming ceremony—the people suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: In his province he levied without measure; when Gaozu's coffin passed through on its way to the tomb, Xin stripped officials and commoners alike to fund the reception, and the people groaned under it.

sentences.zh: 初，聞殺楊邠、史宏肇，遽啟宴席，集參佐賓幕，令相致賀。

translations.literal: At first, when he heard that Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao had been killed, he hastily opened a feast, gathered his staff and secretariat guests, and had them offer congratulations to one another.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao had been killed, he at once threw a banquet, gathered his staff and secretariat advisers, and told them to congratulate one another.

sentences.zh: 曰：「我謂天無眼，令我三年不能適意。

translations.literal: He said: "I thought Heaven had no eyes, keeping me from satisfaction for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I used to think Heaven was blind—three years I could not do as I pleased.

sentences.zh: 主上孤立，幾落賊手。

translations.literal: The sovereign stood alone and nearly fell into the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stood alone and nearly fell into the rebels' clutches.

sentences.zh: 諸公勸我一杯可也。

translations.literal: You gentlemen may urge me to take a cup—that will do.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen, you may press a cup on me—that will do.

sentences.zh: 」俄蕭墻之變，憂不能食。

translations.literal: " Soon came the turmoil within the palace walls, and in his anxiety he could not eat.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long came the palace upheaval, and he was too anxious to eat.

sentences.zh: 尋有太后令，言立湘陰公，即令其子往徐州奉迎。

translations.literal: Before long there was an order from the empress dowager saying that the Duke of Xiangyin was to be established as heir; he at once sent his son to Xuzhou to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the dowager issued an order to install the Duke of Xiangyin as heir, and Xin immediately sent his son to Xuzhou to escort him.

sentences.zh: 數日，陳思讓率馬軍經過城西，但令供頓，不敢出城。

translations.literal: Several days later Chen Siran led the horse guard past the west of the city; Xin only ordered provisions supplied and did not dare leave the city.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Chen Siran marched the horse guard past the west wall; Xin supplied their rations but dared not leave the city.

sentences.zh: 未幾，澶州軍變，王峻遣前申州刺史馬鐸領軍赴州巡檢，鐸引軍入城，信惶惑自殺。

translations.literal: Before long there was a mutiny in the army at Dazhou; Wang Jun sent the former prefect of Shenzhou Ma Duo to lead troops to the prefecture on an inspection tour, and Duo led his army into the city; Xin, in panic and confusion, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, the Dazhou garrison mutinied; Wang Jun sent the former Shen prefect Ma Duo to inspect the prefecture, and Duo marched into the city—whereupon Xin, distraught, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，追封蔡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangshun era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun reign he was posthumously created Prince of Cai.

sentences.zh: 湘陰公赟，為徐州節度使。

translations.literal: The Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, was military governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, held the Xuzhou military governorship.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年八月中，有雲見五色。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Qianyou, clouds appeared in five colors.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Qianyou 1, five-colored clouds were seen.

sentences.zh: 明年冬杪，有鳥翔集於鮮碧堂庭樹，黃質朱喙，金目青翼，紺趾黑尾，有類於鳳。

translations.literal: At the end of winter the next year a bird alighted on a tree in the courtyard of the Fresh Green Hall: yellow body, vermilion beak, golden eyes, blue-green wings, dark purple feet and black tail—rather like a phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Late the following winter a bird settled on a tree in the Fresh Green Hall courtyard—yellow-bodied, vermilion-beaked, with golden eyes, blue-green wings, violet feet, and a black tail, rather like a phoenix.

sentences.zh: 有賓佐嘆曰：「野鳥入室，主人將去。

translations.literal: A staff member sighed and said: "When a wild bird enters the house, the master is about to depart.
translations.idiomatic: One of his advisers sighed and said, "When a wild bird flies indoors, the master is about to leave.

sentences.zh: 」旬浹而不知所之。

translations.literal: " After ten days and more it vanished, no one knew where.
translations.idiomatic: " Ten days later it was gone, and no one knew where.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年冬十一月，周太祖駐軍於京師，議立嗣君，奉太后誥，立赟為嗣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter in the third year of Qianyou, Zhou Taizu stationed his army at the capital, deliberated on establishing an heir, and in accordance with the dowager's patent established Yun as successor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Qianyou 3, Zhou Taizu camped at the capital to choose an heir; obeying the dowager's patent, he named Yun successor.

sentences.zh: 傳誥之際，馮道笏墜於地，左右惡之。

translations.literal: At the moment the patent was transmitted, Feng Dao's court tablet fell to the ground, and those beside him regarded it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: As the patent was read out, Feng Dao's tablet slipped to the floor—those around him took it as a bad sign.

sentences.zh: 馮道至，赟出郊迎，常所乘馬比甚馴服，至是馬蹄嚙奔逸，人不可制，乃以他馬代之，時以為不祥。

translations.literal: When Feng Dao arrived, Yun went out to the suburbs to welcome him; the horse he usually rode had always been very docile, but this time it bit at its bit and bolted, beyond human control, so another horse was substituted—at the time this was taken as inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Dao arrived, Yun rode out to meet him; the horse he always used had been thoroughly tame, but now it champed the bit and bolted beyond control, so they switched mounts—people read it as an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 將離彭城，嘗一日，天有白光一道自西來，照城中如晝，有聲如雷，時人謂之天裂；

translations.literal: As he was about to leave Pengcheng, on one day a streak of white light came from the west, illuminating the city as if at noon, with a sound like thunder—people of the time called it a rending of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of leaving Pengcheng, one day a shaft of white light shot in from the west and lit the city like noon, with a thunderous roar—folk called it Heaven splitting;

sentences.zh: 又有巨星墜於徐野，殷然有聲，或謂之天狗。

translations.literal: there was also a great star that fell on the Xuzhou plain with a deep rumbling sound, and some called it the Heavenly Dog.
translations.idiomatic: and a great star crashed on the Xuzhou plain with a deep boom—some called it the Heavenly Dog.

sentences.zh: 後赟果廢死。

translations.literal: Later Yun was indeed deposed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was indeed later deposed and killed.

sentences.zh: （案：《湘陰公傳》原本殘闕，考《十國春秋·湘陰公傳》云：湘陰公赟，世祖子也，高祖愛之，以為己子。

translations.literal: (Note: the original text of the 《Biography of the Duke of Xiangyin》 is defective; consulting the 《Biography of the Duke of Xiangyin》 in the Ten States Spring and Autumn, it says: the Duke of Xiangyin Yun was a son of Shizu; Gaozu loved him and treated him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: (Editor's note: the base 《Biography of the Duke of Xiangyin》 is corrupt; the 《Ten States Spring and Autumn》 account reads: the Duke of Xiangyin Yun was a son of Shizu; Gaozu doted on him and raised him as his own.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年，拜武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyou he was appointed military governor of the Wuning circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyou 1 he was made military governor of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 二年，加同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was given the additional title of Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 郭威既敗慕容彥超於北郊，隱帝遇弒，威入京師，謂諸大臣密相推戴，及見宰相馮道等，道殊無意。

translations.literal: After Guo Wei had defeated Murong Yanchao at the northern suburb and the Hidden Emperor met assassination, Wei entered the capital and told the chief ministers to confer secretly on enthroning him; when he met the chief councilor Feng Dao and others, Dao showed no intention at all.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Wei routed Murong Yanchao north of the capital and Emperor Yin was murdered, Wei entered the city and asked the chief ministers to back him in secret; when he met Feng Dao and the rest, Dao showed no inclination whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 威不得已，見道下拜，而道猶受拜如平時，徐勞之曰：「公行良苦。

translations.literal: Wei had no choice; he met Dao and bowed, yet Dao still received the bow as in ordinary times and slowly comforted him, saying: "Your journey has been truly arduous.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had no choice but to bow to Dao; Dao accepted the bow as usual and said slowly, "You have had a hard road of it.

sentences.zh: 」威意色皆沮，以為大臣未有推己意，又難於自立，因與王峻入白太后，推擇漢嗣。

translations.literal: " Wei's expression and color were altogether dejected; he thought the great ministers had not yet shown intent to support him, and that it was again difficult to establish himself on his own; he therefore entered with Wang Jun to report to the empress dowager and have a Han heir chosen.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei's face fell; he took it that the ministers were not yet backing him and that seizing the throne on his own would be hard, so he and Wang Jun went in to the dowager to have a Later Han heir selected.

sentences.zh: 群臣乃共奏曰：「武寧節度使赟，高祖愛以為子，宜立為嗣。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers then jointly memorialized, saying: "The military governor of Wuning, Yun, whom Gaozu loved and treated as a son, should be established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers jointly memorialized: "Wuning governor Yun, whom Gaozu loved as a son, should be made heir.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣太師馮道率百官往迎，道揣威意不在赟，直前問曰：「公此舉由衷乎？

translations.literal: " They then sent Grand Preceptor Feng Dao at the head of the hundred officials to welcome him; Dao guessed that Wei's mind was not on Yun, stepped forward and asked: "Is this move of yours from the heart?
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Preceptor Feng Dao was sent at the head of the bureaucracy to escort him; sensing that Wei did not mean Yun, Dao stepped forward and asked, "Does this come from your heart?

sentences.zh: 」威指天為誓。

translations.literal: " Wei pointed to Heaven and swore.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei swore by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 道既行，語左右曰：「吾生平不能謬語人，今謬語矣。

translations.literal: After Dao had set out, he said to those beside him: "All my life I have been unable to speak falsely to people; today I have spoken falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road, Dao told his attendants, "I have never lied to anyone in my life—today I have lied.

sentences.zh: 」道見，傳太后意召之。

translations.literal: " When Dao met him, he conveyed the dowager's intent and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " When Dao met Yun, he relayed the dowager's summons.

sentences.zh: 赟行至宋州，威已自澶州為兵士擁還京師。

translations.literal: When Yun reached Songzhou, Wei had already been escorted back to the capital from Dazhou by the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yun reached Songzhou while Wei had already been carried back to the capital from Dazhou by his troops.

sentences.zh: 王峻慮赟左右生變，遣侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇威以兵七百騎衛赟。

translations.literal: Wang Jun feared that those around Yun might stir up trouble, and sent the commander of the palace horse guard Guo Chongwei with seven hundred horsemen to guard Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun feared trouble from Yun's entourage and sent palace horse-guard commander Guo Chongwei with seven hundred cavalry to escort him.

sentences.zh: 崇威至宋州，赟登樓問崇威所以來之意，崇威曰：「澶州軍變，懼未察之，遣崇威護衛，非惡意也。

translations.literal: When Chongwei reached Songzhou, Yun ascended a tower and asked the purpose of Chongwei's coming; Chongwei said: "There was a mutiny in the army at Dazhou; fearing you had not grasped it, they sent Chongwei to guard you—there is no ill intent.
translations.idiomatic: At Songzhou, Yun climbed a tower and asked why Chongwei had come; Chongwei said, "The Dazhou garrison mutinied—we feared you had not heard and sent me to guard you, not to harm you.

sentences.zh: 」瑽召崇威，崇威不敢進。

translations.literal: " Yun summoned Chongwei, but Chongwei did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: " Yun summoned him, but Chongwei dared not come up.

sentences.zh: 馮道出與崇威語，崇威乃登樓見赟。

translations.literal: Feng Dao went out to speak with Chongwei, and only then did Chongwei ascend the tower to see Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao went out to speak with him, and only then did Chongwei mount the tower to see Yun.

sentences.zh: 時護聖指揮使張令超帥步兵為赟宿衛，判官董裔說赟曰：「觀崇威瞻視舉措，必有異謀。

translations.literal: At that time the commander of the Inspired Guard Zhang Lingchao led foot soldiers to camp as Yun's night guard; the administrative aide Dong Yi urged Yun, saying: "Judging from Chongwei's looks and movements, he must have some other design.
translations.idiomatic: Inspired Guard commander Zhang Lingchao led infantry on Yun's night watch; aide Dong Yi urged him, "From Chongwei's bearing and movements, he clearly has another plot.

sentences.zh: 道路皆言郭威已為天子，而陛下深入不止，禍其至哉。

translations.literal: Everyone on the road says Guo Wei is already Son of Heaven, yet Your Majesty presses deeper without stopping—will not disaster soon arrive?
translations.idiomatic: Travelers all say Guo Wei is already emperor, yet you press on—will disaster not soon arrive?

sentences.zh: 請急召令超，諭以禍福，使夜以兵劫崇威所屬士卒，明日掠睢陽金帛，募士卒，北走太原。

translations.literal: I beg you urgently to summon Lingchao, explain the fortune or ruin to him, and have him by night with troops seize the soldiers under Chongwei's command; tomorrow plunder the gold and silks of Suiyang, recruit soldiers, and flee north to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Summon Lingchao at once, show him the stakes, and have him seize Chongwei's men by night; tomorrow strip Suiyang of gold and silk, raise troops, and flee north to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 彼新定京邑，未暇追我，此策之上也。

translations.literal: They have newly secured the capital and will have no leisure to pursue us—this is the best stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: They will have just taken the capital and will not have time to chase us—that is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 」赟猶豫未決。

translations.literal: " Yun hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: " Yun wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 是夕，崇威密誘令超歸郭氏，盡奪赟部下兵。

translations.literal: That evening Chongwei secretly induced Lingchao to return to Guo's side and stripped Yun of all the troops under his command.
translations.idiomatic: That night Chongwei secretly won Lingchao to Guo Wei and stripped Yun of every soldier.

sentences.zh: 郭威以書召道先歸，留其副趙上交、王度奉赟入朝太后，道乃辭赟先還。

translations.literal: Guo Wei with a letter summoned Dao to return first, leaving his deputies Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du to escort Yun to an audience with the empress dowager; Dao then took leave of Yun and returned ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei summoned Dao back by letter, leaving deputies Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du to escort Yun to the dowager; Dao took leave of Yun and went ahead.

sentences.zh: 赟謂道曰：「寡人此來，所恃者以公三十年舊相，是以不疑。

translations.literal: Yun said to Dao: "In coming here, what I relied on was that you are a minister of thirty years' standing—therefore I did not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Yun told Dao, "I came trusting you as my minister of thirty years—that is why I never doubted.

sentences.zh: 」道默然。

translations.literal: " Dao was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Dao said nothing.

sentences.zh: 赟客將賈貞等數目道，欲圖之，赟曰：「勿草草，事豈出於公耶！

translations.literal: Yun's guest officers Jia Zhen and others eyed Dao several times, intending to plot against him; Yun said: "Do not act rashly—how could the affair have come from the duke!
translations.idiomatic: Yun's staff officers Jia Zhen and others eyed Dao, ready to strike; Yun said, "Do not be hasty—surely this is not his doing!

sentences.zh: 」道已去，崇威乃幽赟於外館，殺賈貞、董裔及牙內都虞候劉福、孔目官夏昭度等。

translations.literal: " After Dao had gone, Chongwei then confined Yun in an outer lodge and killed Jia Zhen, Dong Yi, the inner headquarters deputy commander Liu Fu, the clerical officer Xia Zhaodu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Dao was gone, Chongwei locked Yun in an outer lodge and killed Jia Zhen, Dong Yi, inner headquarters deputy Liu Fu, clerical officer Xia Zhaodu, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 郭威已監國。

translations.literal: Guo Wei had already become regent of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei was already regent.

sentences.zh: 太后乃下詔曰：「比者，樞密使威，誌安宗社，議立長君，以徐州節度使赟，高祖親近，立為漢嗣，乃自藩鎮，召赴京師。

translations.literal: The empress dowager then issued an edict, saying: "Recently the commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wei, wishing to settle the altars of state, deliberated on establishing a mature sovereign; taking the military governor of Xuzhou Yun, whom Gaozu held close, he established him as Han heir and summoned him from his military province to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager then issued an edict: "Recently Commissioner Wei, seeking to secure the realm, chose a mature ruler; Xuzhou governor Yun, close to Gaozu, was named Han heir and summoned from his province to the capital.

sentences.zh: 雖誥命已行，而軍情不附。

translations.literal: Although the patent command had already been issued, the army's sentiment did not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Though the patent had gone out, the armies would not follow him.

sentences.zh: 天道在北，人心靡東，適當改卜之初，俾應分士之命。

translations.literal: Heaven's Way lies in the north, and men's hearts do not turn east; it happens to be the beginning of a change in divination, so let him answer to the mandate of allotted territory.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate lies in the north, hearts will not turn east—at this moment of changing the augury, let him take the fate allotted to his rank.

sentences.zh: 赟可降授開府儀同三司、檢校太師、上柱國，封湘陰公。

translations.literal: Yun may be demoted and granted Acting Third Rank, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Supreme Pillar of State, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yun is demoted to Acting Third Rank, honorary Grand Preceptor, Supreme Pillar of State, and enfeoffed Duke of Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 」赟卒以殺死。

translations.literal: " In the end Yun died by killing.
translations.idiomatic: " Yun was ultimately killed.

sentences.zh: 《五代史補》：郭忠恕，七歲童子及第，富有文學，尤工篆隸。

translations.literal: 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Guo Zhongshu, at age seven a child prodigy who passed the examination, was rich in literary learning and especially skilled in seal and clerical scripts.
translations.idiomatic: 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Guo Zhongshu passed the child-examination at seven, was deeply learned, and excelled at seal and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 嘗有人於龍山得鳥跡篆，忠恕一見，輒誦如宿習。

translations.literal: Once someone obtained bird-track seal script on Long Mountain; at one glance Zhongshu recited it as if from long familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: Someone once found bird-track seal script on Long Mountain; Zhongshu read it at a glance as though he had studied it for years.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，湘陰公鎮徐州，辟為推官。

translations.literal: During Qianyou the Duke of Xiangyin held Xuzhou and recruited him as investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou, while the Duke of Xiangyin governed Xuzhou, he was hired as investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 周祖之入京師也，少主崩於北岡，周主命宰相馮道迎湘陰公，將立之。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder entered the capital, the young lord died on the northern ridge; the Zhou ruler ordered the chief councilor Feng Dao to welcome the Duke of Xiangyin, intending to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder entered the capital, the young emperor died on the northern ridge; the Zhou ruler ordered Feng Dao to escort the Duke of Xiangyin and install him.

sentences.zh: 至宋州，高祖已為三軍推戴。

translations.literal: When they reached Songzhou, Gaozu had already been pushed forward by the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: At Songzhou, Gaozu had already been acclaimed by the three armies.

sentences.zh: 忠恕知事變，乃正色責道曰：「令公累朝大臣，誠信著於天下，四方談士，無賢不肖皆以為長者，今一旦返作脫空漢，前功業並棄，令公之心安乎？

translations.literal: Zhongshu knew affairs had changed and sternly reproached Dao, saying: "Your Grace is a minister through successive reigns; sincerity and trust are renowned throughout the realm; scholars everywhere, worthy or not, all regard you as an elder—now in a single morning you turn into a hollow fraud, casting away your former achievements together—does Your Grace's heart rest at ease?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu saw how matters stood and rebuked Dao to his face: "You are a minister of many reigns, trusted throughout the realm; scholars everywhere, worthy or not, call you an elder—yet in a morning you become a hollow fraud and throw away a lifetime's standing—can your conscience be at ease?

sentences.zh: 」道無言對。

translations.literal: " Dao had no words in reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Dao had no answer.

sentences.zh: 忠恕因勸湘陰公殺道以奔河東，公猶豫未決，遂及於禍。

translations.literal: Zhongshu therefore urged the Duke of Xiangyin to kill Dao and flee to Hedong; the duke hesitated and could not decide, and thus met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu then urged the duke to kill Dao and flee to Hedong; the duke wavered, and disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 忠恕竄跡久之，晚年尤好輕忽，卒以此敗，坐除名配流焉。）〉

translations.literal: Zhongshu hid himself for a long time; in his later years he especially loved to treat things lightly, and in the end failed because of this, suffering removal from office and banishment by assignment.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu hid for years; in old age he grew especially reckless and finally fell because of it, stripped of rank and exiled.) End of editorial note.)〉
